Definition: perhaps as the same as G2042; properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication) faction:--contention(-ious), strife.
BiblicalUsage: Eritheía is selfish ambition — the party spirit, the intrigue that builds a faction. Paul names it among the works of the flesh, and James says where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work. It is the word for ambition that serves itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe eritheía is the most respectable sin in the church: ambition dressed up as zeal. I hold that the cure is the mind of Christ, who made Himself of no reputation.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
